items.text: Regarding the predictability of human behavior:

options.A: Human behavior contains irreducible complexity that resists full prediction
options.B: Individual behavior is complex but has discoverable patterns
options.C: Behavior is predictable in aggregate but not for individuals
options.D: Given enough information, most behavior is fundamentally predictable
options.E: People are simple—they want status, security, and pleasure

items.text: A philanthropist is discovered to have also engaged in tax fraud. How do you make sense of this?

options.A: Humans contain genuine multitudes—contradictory traits coexist naturally
options.B: People are complex but there's usually an underlying explanation
options.C: This reveals compartmentalization—different contexts, different behavior
options.D: One of these traits is the "real" person; the other is a mask
options.E: This is unusual—most people are consistently good or bad

items.text: To truly understand another person requires:

options.A: Accepting that full understanding is ultimately impossible
options.B: Years of deep interaction, and still incomplete knowledge
options.C: Careful observation and empathy over extended time
options.D: Understanding their core motivations and formative history
options.E: Recognizing their type and basic drives
